kibana.alert.rule.author: ACME
_source.kibana.alert.rule.description: Detects a NAXSI web-application-firewall block (event.type denied) where the offending content was in a request argument or body (zones ARGS/BODY) and the cumulative NAXSI score was 50 or higher. Low-score URL-zone matches (rule 1000, score 8, mostly static file names containing SQL keywords) are excluded, so what remains is a real SQLi/XSS/RCE-style payload that the WAF stopped. Baseline on 2026-10-05: ~8.7k such blocks/day but from only 6 IPs against 7 vhosts; with suppression this yields a handful of alerts/day.
_source.kibana.alert.rule.name: WAF: Injection Payload Blocked in Request Parameters or Body
_source.kibana.alert.rule.note:
### Investigation Steps
1. Open the alert: `source.ip`, `url.domain`, `url.path`, `rule.id`, `nginx.naxsi.zone`, `nginx.naxsi.var_name` and `nginx.naxsi.score`. NAXSI rule ids: 1000-1009 SQL, 1010-1011 obvious RFI, 1013-1015 directory traversal, 1100-1101 RFI/XSS, 1200 evading tricks, 1302-1315 XSS/format string, 11/12 body/args malformed.
2. Look at `event.original` for the raw request line and the matched variable.
3. Pivot on `source.ip` in the access log (event.type: access): did the same client get any 200 responses to the same path or to other sensitive paths? A 200 after a block attempt means the attacker may have found a bypass.
4. Volume from one IP against one vhost = automated scanner (sqlmap, nuclei); block the IP. Low volume with hand-crafted payloads = targeted; notify the site owner.

### False positives
Legitimate forms that submit HTML or SQL-looking text (CMS editors, code snippets). Tune via NAXSI whitelist for that vhost rather than disabling this rule.
